text:
We checked “RollUp_Bad” and found 7 issues in the InDesign file that are likely causing the problems in Frontify, plus 4 that may change how it looks. Here’s what to change:

Likely causing the problems

1. Text frame has no paragraph style
Frontify uses paragraph styles to format text and decide what can be edited.
Where: text frames “Columns”, “SUMMER” (page 1)
• Select the frame and apply a paragraph style in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles (any style except [Basic Paragraph] or [No Paragraph Style]).
Learn more

2. Threaded (linked) text frames
Frontify doesn’t support text flowing from one frame into another.
Where: the text frame “COLLECTION” (page 1)
• Turn on View > Extras > Show Text Threads, then double-click a frame’s out port to break the thread so each frame holds its own text.
Learn more

3. Embedded image
Frontify needs images as separate linked files and can’t read images embedded in the document.
Where: the image “album.png” (page 1)
• In Window > Links, select the image and choose Unembed Link from the panel menu.
• Save it into the Links folder and package again.
Learn more

4. Image frame is flipped or skewed
Frontify can’t reproduce flipped or skewed frames, so the image will look different or break when edited.
Where: the image “monobrand-text-logo-black.png” (page 1)
• Select the image frame and choose Object > Transform > Clear Transformations (or set the shear angle to 0° and remove the flip).
Learn more

5. Pasted graphic
Graphics pasted straight into InDesign aren’t linked files, so Frontify can’t read them.
• Save the graphic as a file (for example SVG, PDF or PNG), delete the pasted version and place the file with File > Place.
Learn more

6. Text frame has columns
Frontify doesn’t support multiple columns inside one text frame.
Where: the text frame “Columns” (page 1)
• Set Columns to 1 in Object > Text Frame Options. Use separate text frames if you need columns.
Learn more

7. Unsupported font format
Frontify can only use OpenType (.otf) and TrueType (.ttf) fonts.
Where: the font “Futura copy.ttc”
• Get an OTF or TTF version from the font vendor and swap it in with Type > Find/Replace Font.
Learn more

May change how it looks

8. Document has bleed
Bleed is added to every export, which is right for print templates but usually unwanted for digital ones.
Current bleed: 1 mm on all sides
• For a digital template, set bleed to 0 in File > Document Setup > Bleed and Slug. For print templates, bleed is fine.
Learn more

9. Image frame is rotated
Rotation works, but the frame may look slightly different in Frontify than in InDesign.
Where: the image “Logo-Circle_new.svg” (page 1, rotated 90°)
• Check the result in Frontify. If it looks off, remove the rotation from the frame.
Learn more

10. Paragraph Composer used
The Adobe Paragraph Composer breaks lines differently from browsers, so text may reflow in Frontify.
Where: the paragraph style “[Basic Paragraph]”, used on page 1
• In the paragraph style, go to Justification and set Composer to Adobe Single-line Composer.
Learn more

11. Unused images in the package
These files aren’t used in the document and only make the package bigger.
Where: the image “music.svg”
• Delete the unused files from the Links folder before zipping the package.
Learn more

Worth a quick check (often fine as is)

12. Large image
Very large images slow down editing and exporting in Frontify.
Where: the image “iStock-1226023798.jpg” (page 1, 15.25 MB)
• Reduce the image’s pixel size or file size if it doesn’t need to be this large.
Learn more

Once that’s done, package the document again with File > Package, zip the package folder and upload it to Frontify.
